# Immutable rows: once written, never updated or deleted

> Sequelize disables the `updatedAt` and `deletedAt` timestamps on the [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) model, making each ledger entry immutable once inserted.

_Part of [Immutable ledger entry row](ledger-entry-row.md)_

The [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) Sequelize model sets `updatedAt: false` and `deletedAt: false`, disabling ORM update and soft-delete timestamps. Only `createdAt` is available, recording when the entry was written. This configuration enforces a critical invariant: ledger entries are immutable once inserted. No UPDATE, no DELETE, no modification—only CREATE and READ. This permanence is the foundation of a reliable financial ledger.

**Look at:** [`LedgerEntry` in ledger-entry.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/ledger-entry.model.ts#L79)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `LedgerEntry table` | Stores immutable entry rows; only INSERT and SELECT operations are performed |

## Watch out

- There is no `updatedAt` field to track modifications—only `createdAt` exists
- Without soft-delete (`deletedAt: false`), rows cannot be hidden; any deletion is truly permanent
- The model's immutability is enforced at the ORM level; corrections or reversals must be handled by creating new entries
- Downstream systems should assume ledger entries never change; cache and index strategies need to account for this
